blocks.title: Comments on the stadium
blocks.question: Share anything else you have to say about the experience in the stadium.
items: Food and drinks are expensive. Supporters section needs more information widely spread, people break open the locked seats at every game and they don't understand that they purchased GA tix. Away fans have been in the supporters section multiple times.

Food is overpriced, but there are good choices. The audio is horrible. The announcer/music is completely unintelligible. There were issues keeping people from mobbing players in the supporters section
Hope they use a different ticketing agency other than Ticketmaster.

Security could be better. Water stations aren't always there. Parking is too expensive and the attendants sometimes try to prevent us from parking with our Sirens tailgating group for no apparent reason.
Security could do  A better job of responding to incidents. Food is expensive and small portions.

The supporters section often gets inundated after a game wanting signatures. It is chaotic and people push and can get hurt. Also, there are not clear policies for away fans sitting in supporters section and it can get heated.

Too many questions ask too many questions. Food & drink pretty pricey but water readily available in Club. The way our stadium is set up the Supporters section isn’t loud enough compared to other stadiums (thinking Thorns/Reign, etc). Needs to be miked up!

takeaways: Ticketing mostly got good marks: 12 of 15 said prices were fair, 11 rated their ticket rep well, and 10 would recommend season tickets on value alone.
Benefits were the weak spot. 8 of 15 said season tickets didn't come with good benefits.
9 of 15 said stadium food and drink weren't affordable.
Nobody said security responds well to incidents: 9 of 14 weren't sure and 5 said no.
With 15 responses, each answer is about 7% of the total, so read these as signals, not settled numbers.

blocks.title: Comments on Sirens membership
blocks.question: What else would you like us to know about Sirens membership?
items: After the result of the election, I honestly did not know where the Sirens are at. I know it is not a political type of organization. However as a lesbian, I would like to support and be in one that supports that part of me.
Chants/songs should be available on Discord so other supporters throughout stadium can join in
Discord was too hard for me to figure out.  Is it possible to have distinct sections for selling tickets;  comments on games, coaching; watch parties; special sirens events?
Focusing too much lately on activism
Happy to support such a great group of people. Sirens make the home games so enjoyable - happy to be a member.

I have been extremely unhappy with the feed and disrespect on the insta from the Siren members.  We are a support group and I don't feel this group is supportive at all.  People in this group act like they are entitled to know information that is simply none of our business.  They post negative and personal attacks on people who work at The Wave.  This is not the role of a supporters group.  We should be talking about the game and about soccer.  Not about politics and unfounded attacks and allegations that have NOTHING to do with us.  We should be complaining about our teams lack of speed.  Our teams lack of discipline.  Our outside defenders who won't mark.  Our midfield which cannot create any transition with controlled play.  The fact that we don't (although with our newest addition) a finishing forward.  We should NOT be talking politics, social justice or activism.  This is a game.  A sport.  FUN.  I am seriously considering quitting the Sirens because no one wants to discuss the team and the game of soccer, instead they want to bash people.  I think the president and the board need to re-establish the focus and the role of this group.  That role should be a supportive group of The San Diego Wave.  And, lets be real: the only reason people are negative and angry is because we weren't winning this year.  Everyone loves a winner, but the true colors come out when a team is losing.  I don't identify and don't want to be a part of a group of people who are vigilantes intent on bashing and representing people when they are uninformed and have a false sense of entitlement.  I want to surround myself with people who just want to watch soccer, or any sport, and have a constructive a fun time.  I am disappointed the president and the board have chosen to allow this group to run outside the scope of a fan club and turn this into a political social media account.

I hope the Sirens will update the language around its membership and mission because it very much feels performative right now. Sirens say it's a space to support players off the field and build community, but the Discord feels like an echo chamber of the same 15 people. 15 people communicating is worth it, don't get me wrong, but when choices and decisions are made primarily through this platform, it really doesn't feel like it's representative. Aside from Discord, there are no ways for members to know who has said what, so even when/if info is collected in other spaces, members on Discord have no idea. In this vein, I would have liked more transparency and shared communication/meeting notes from the Officers. Holding the Sirens Officers accountable feels like an impossible task to attempt because any signs of concern are taken as personal affronts. Who have the Sirens stood up for this year? Who, in the community or in the club, have Sirens actually taken a stand for? And not only taken a stand, but taken the necessary follow up actions (because sending one email saying the Wave needs to explain themselves and then literally not sending any follow up emails... C'mon, you guys, that's just common sense)? The most community involvement I saw was following the horrendous regional flood and I thought that was great because it demonstrated who the Sirens project to be.... But what about other relevant community and global human and civil rights issues? The silence from the SG this year has, unfortunately, been incredibly loud for several of us; so maybe change what the Sirens proport to stand for, because as is, it's false marketing.
I love the leadership of this group! I’m glad to be a part of the Sirens!

I think the Sirens have been overly involved and I appropriately so with the office politics and the drama surrounding many things this season. I don’t feel that is the role of the sirens and while comments and statements can be made they may not reflect all sirens or fans and our involvement or perceived entitlement to know or be connected to club politics and even investigations is an overstep. Build community, yes please, create a safe fun space in the cove, yes please, but it feels exclusive sometimes to be a siren and more about the drama than the joy of the game and the team we love. I realize this season has been hard and I have my own opinions but I discuss them individually and don’t think leadership in siren’s or the sirens themselves are a platform to meddle. That said accountability for concerns in terms of sharing them up is valuable but we or rather I feel we are not police or enforcers and I think we can reflect values that do not overstep.

I understand that there have been some lawsuits and other things between the wave employees and the wave management. I somehow get the feeling that the sirens leaders are interacting with wave management and it’s not clear how they are getting direction on that. When the sirens are publishing things on social media making statements about wave management, it is unclear how they came to the conclusion that that’s what the siren members wanted. I’m not saying what they did is wrong or not approved of by a lot of people, but it’s just really unclear who is making decisions about that kind of stuff.
I wish there were other ways to engage than Discord.
I'm really happy to support the Sirens, but I'm not super involved. Hopefully that's o.k., I enjoyed getting the newsletters and supporting the Wave!

It is not worth it. I have met multiple officers multiple times over 2 years, had conversations with them, etc. and they never recognize me and continue to ask if I want to join. We are paying members and are told we can’t move beyond a point UNLESS you know an officer and they are ok with you doing that. We aren’t included in some wave events with you so sometimes that is our only opportunity, especially kids, to meet players and I watched as people were basically told “oh we’ve seen you standing here the whole game but to get your Sheridan jersey signed you need to go to a different section. You can’t cross the pink tape.” Like what?! They have no chance at that point. They are paying siren members and you guys act like the council is high and mighty. It’s recognized you do the banners and chants and drumming, but a lot of times it seems like you guys want this club to be exclusive to just the officers and their friends. I couldn’t even be apart of the discord this season because the talk about the players is so non constructive and I know as a person who played, would be extremely hurtful. Supporters don’t say such things about the people they supposedly support and I actually feel like a lot of sirens don’t actually like the team or know soccer and just want to be apart of a group. I will still be in the section standing and cheering because that’s where my season tickets are, but I won’t be apart of the sirens group anymore. The $30 isn’t worth it.
Other than, a BIG THANK YOU for making the season more enjoyable during home games.
Since you have the ear of the club, it would be nice to bring up security concerns as I stated above regarding behavior that goes against its own policies and having security follow though.

takeaways: 89 of 97 people feel safe at home games.
Season ticket holders were mostly happy with prices (70 of 80) and their reps (58 of 80), but less sure about benefits: 45 said yes and 27 said no.
52 of 97 said stadium food and drink aren't affordable.
Many people weren't sure how to rate security (65 of 97 picked "Unsure") or dietary options (45 of 97).
The newsletter was the best-liked Sirens activity: 86 of the 96 people it applies to were satisfied. Discounts drew the most shrugs, with 41 of 83 neutral.
Volunteer events (46), social events (44) and social justice and activism (43) topped the list of events people want more of.

takeaways: 58 of 63 people are very likely to renew their Sirens membership.
52 of the 53 people who rated their ticket rep were satisfied, 37 of them very satisfied.
The newsletter (42 of 63) and Discord (41) are how most people hear Sirens news.
FairPlay in North Park (24 of 51) and Novo Brewing in Mission Valley (21) drew the most people to away-game watch parties.
The NWSL Players Association was the most-chosen organization to keep supporting, picked by 49 of 57.
24 of 64 people sit in the Cove (section 138); the rest are spread across the stadium.

rep.title: Ticket rep service, all three years
rep.subtitle: Share of people who rated their rep positively, leaving out "not sure" answers. 2023 and 2024 asked yes or no; 2025 used a satisfaction scale, so "very" and "somewhat satisfied" both count here. The 2025 scale had two satisfied options, one unsatisfied option and no neutral, which makes a high score more likely.
